bib.title: Text Analytics with Python, Chapter 7: Semantic and Sentiment Analysis

question: Can we analyze and understand the meaning and sentiment behind a body of text, using WordNet, word sense disambiguation, NER, logic, supervised classifiers and sentiment lexicons?
contributions: WordNet synsets and lexical relations explored through NLTK
Lesk word sense disambiguation, NLTK and Stanford NER on one Wikipedia paragraph, propositional and first-order logic with theorem provers
Sentiment on 50,000 IMDb reviews: one SVM against SentiWordNet, VADER and Pattern lexicons, with mood and modality

limits: No uncertainty, seeds or repeated runs for any sentiment number; one split of one dataset.
The 35,000/15,000 split is the first 35,000 rows of a pooled 50,000 file; the original IMDb 25k/25k split is not used, and row order is not described.
Lexicon thresholds were chosen on the test data, so lexicon scores are optimistic.
The NER comparison is one paragraph judged by eye with no gold labels; Lesk is shown only on examples it gets right.
The author concedes that sentiment labels overlap and warns against chasing a perfect model.
Dated: Python 2 code (print statements, HTMLParser), SGDClassifier n_iter (now max_iter), Stanford NER 2014 jar via Java, no neural or transformer models, WordNet 3.0-era NLTK.
practices: Reuse the text-classification workflow of Chapter 4 (normalize, vectorize with the training vectorizer, fit, predict, evaluate) for sentiment (Supervised ML section).
Report accuracy, precision, recall, F1, the confusion matrix and the per-class report together, not one or two metrics (Comparing Model Performances).
Do not assume the best model here is best elsewhere: it depends on the data (Comparing Model Performances).
Use lexicons when no labelled data exists (Unsupervised Lexicon-based Techniques).
Tune the sentiment threshold, for example raise SentiWordNet's from 0 to 0.1 or higher, when predictions skew to one class (SentiWordNet section).
Train your own NER tagger on a tagged corpus matched to your text rather than assuming a stock tagger fits (Named Entity Recognition).
